w: Perched on East Gros Ventre Butte overlooking the National Elk Refuge, this 51,000-square-foot museum wears an Idaho quartzite facade inspired by the ruins of Scotland's Slains Castle. Its core collection centers on painters Carl Rungius and Bob Kuhn, spread across 14 galleries and a sculpture trail.
s: A wildlife-art museum modeled on a ruined Scottish castle
_facts: 51,000 sq ft building faced in Idaho quartzite
Facade inspired by the ruins of Slains Castle, Scotland
Centerpiece collection of works by Carl Rungius and Bob Kuhn
14 galleries plus a sculpture trail; over 80,000 visitors yearly

w: Known simply as Town Square, this park at the center of Jackson is framed by four elk-antler arches built from antlers shed at the National Elk Refuge and gathered yearly by Boy Scouts. Once open commons used as an elk thoroughfare, it became a park in the 1920s, dedicated for Washington's 1932 bicentennial.
s: Jackson's town square, framed by four elk-antler arches
_facts: Four elk-antler arches, periodically rebuilt with antlers gathered by Boy Scouts
Formerly open commons used as an elk migration route
Dedicated as a George Washington bicentennial memorial in 1932
Contains a stone memorial to explorer John Colter

n: St. John's Episcopal Church and Rectory
w: This complex of log buildings began in 1911 as a rectory-hostel under Episcopal Bishop Nathaniel Thomas; the church followed in 1916, built by Butch and Ed Robinson from logs cut by George and Clarence Blain. Among the largest log structures in Jackson Hole, it now serves as a chapel since a larger 1995 church.
s: Jackson's largest log church, built by locals in 1916
_facts: Rectory built in 1911 as a hostel and community center
Church built in 1916 by local builders Butch and Ed Robinson
Among the largest log structures in Jackson Hole
Now used as a chapel after a larger church was built in 1995

w: Built by brothers John and Jess Wort on the site of their father's 1915-1932 livery stable, this Tudor-style brick hotel opened in 1941 as Jackson's first luxury lodging. In 1950 it added the Silver Dollar Bar, its surface embedded with 2,032 uncirculated silver dollars from the family's frontier fortune.
s: A 1941 hotel bar with 2,032 silver dollars in its counter
_facts: Opened in 1941 as Jackson's first luxury hotel
Built on the site of the Wort family's 1915-1932 livery stable
Silver Dollar Bar added in 1950, embedded with 2,032 silver dollars
Family previously ran what is now Signal Mountain Lodge in Grand Teton NP

w: Home of Robert Miller, who settled along Flat Creek in 1885, helped organize the town of Jackson in 1901, and ran the Teton Division of the Yellowstone Timberland Reserve from this cabin from 1903. Thanks to rancher S.N. Leek's campaigning, nearly 2,000 acres of his land became the National Elk Refuge in 1912.
s: The cabin behind the founding of the National Elk Refuge
_facts: Home of Robert Miller, who settled here in 1885
Miller helped organize the town of Jackson in 1901
Miller's land formed the National Elk Refuge in 1912
His wife served two terms as mayor of Jackson in the 1920s
